# Factor I O

> Factor I O Co., Ltd. is an independent software studio based in Thailand, building local-first Android apps and AI infrastructure. No advertising, no data collection, no engagement metrics. Founded by Thanat Manasakool.

Factor I O ships two kinds of thing: consumer Android apps that keep data on the
device, and developer infrastructure extracted from Light, the internal AI stack
the studio runs on. The best-documented public component is light-tools.

## Open source

- [light-tools](https://studio.factor-io.com/light-tools.html): Open-source MCP server that replaces the built-in file and shell tools used by AI coding agents with token-efficient versions. One Go binary, stdio, no daemon or database. Five tools: light_file, light_bash, light_ssh, light_scp, light_ops. Installs via `npm install --global @factor-i-o/light-tools`. GPL-3.0-or-later.
- [light-tools source](https://github.com/icediceice/light-tools): Canonical repository, README, releases and checksums.
- [light-tools reference](https://github.com/icediceice/light-tools/blob/main/docs/REFERENCE.md): Exact tool and verb semantics — argument repair, continuation cursors, output spill, snapshots, confinement.
- [light-tools agent setup](https://github.com/icediceice/light-tools/blob/main/AGENT-SETUP.md): Full registration procedure for MCP-capable coding agents.
- [light-tools security model](https://github.com/icediceice/light-tools/blob/main/SECURITY.md): What `allowed_roots` does and does not protect. Read before treating confinement as a security boundary.

## Tools

- [AI Inference TCO Calculator](https://studio.factor-io.com/tco-calculator.html): Conversation-led decision support that sizes an inference workload from its USER COUNT rather than a token total nobody can supply, then compares self-hosting, a cloud model API and rented GPU nodes over a default 60-month horizon. A guided interview asks eight questions — workload, scale, usage intensity, placement, data boundary, workflow, fallback and horizon — and every answer maps to an allowlisted real control. Answering changes nothing until Apply, which writes the answers through the same validated path and triggers one deterministic recompute. Any single question can be sent to MiniMax-M3 for help; the model explains the trade-off and may mark a suggested option, but it never selects one, and a returned recommendation must name an option that question actually offers. A separate explicit post-Apply turn produces a Nutanix-biased local-LLM specification with Kubernetes/Linux-VM equivalents, grounded in a deterministic component ledger that explains demand, sizing, recurring, one-time, subscription, routing and exclusion paths without delegating arithmetic to AI. Source and engine arithmetic remain exact USD; inputs, every calculator money surface and exports are THB through a dated exact rational FX boundary. Startup atomically refreshes complete OpenRouter pricing and Frankfurter ECB-mirror FX, preserving dated digest-pinned fallbacks when a source is partial or unavailable. There is no API-key field: AI requests go to Factor I O's own endpoint at ai.factor-io.com, which holds the MiniMax credential server-side, forwards the request and returns the reply unmodified — so Factor I O DOES proxy calculator AI requests, though it stores neither the request nor the response and logs only route, status, model, byte counts and duration. Before each AI POST the page still builds a copyable credential-free request for your own gateway, Ollama or LM Studio; bounded complete history stays in current-tab memory and AI prose never enters math/provenance/export/print. Demand binds on the peak second, payback is a whole number of months or does_not_converge with a reason, arithmetic is decimal-exact and every number carries provenance. Refresh snapshots with `node scripts/refresh-pricing.mjs`. Zero build step, no analytics or tracking. Normative spec: docs/tco-calculator/SPEC.md.

## Products

- [Blink](https://blink.factor-io.com/): Privacy protection for Android, built for the threat standing next to you. Entirely on-device, zero data collection. Live on Android.
- [Blink privacy policy](https://blink.factor-io.com/privacy-policy): Blink's own policy, separate from the studio-wide statement.
- CatCountdown: A countdown app with personality — nine cats, fifteen categories. Launching soon on Google Play and iOS.

## About

- [Factor I O studio](https://studio.factor-io.com/): Products, approach, services and contact.
- [Privacy statement](https://studio.factor-io.com/privacy.html): Studio-wide policy — no advertising, tracking or Factor I O data collection. The calculator automatically GETs public OpenRouter pricing and Frankfurter FX without calculator context; conversation/context is POSTed only when the visitor explicitly presses Send or Ask, directly to the endpoint they configured. Token and history remain in current-tab memory and Factor I O does not receive or proxy them.
- [Thanat Manasakool on LinkedIn](https://www.linkedin.com/in/thanat-manasakool-3101905a/): Founder & Principal Engineer. 20+ years in enterprise infrastructure, including five years as an Ecosystem Solutions Architect for Red Hat and Nutanix.
- [Thanat Manasakool on GitHub](https://github.com/icediceice): Maintainer of light-tools.
